title: Reducedness ascends along a regular map of Noetherian rings
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $A$ is reduced (every nilpotent element of $A$ is zero) and $\varphi$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Then $B$ is reduced (every nilpotent element of $B$ is zero).

proof.text: Unfold regularity of $\varphi$ using [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The map $A\to B$ is flat, and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the ring $F_{\mathfrak p}=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Take a universe-lifted copy of the degree-one finite purely inseparable extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ in this definition. The canonical identification $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}F_{\mathfrak p}\cong F_{\mathfrak p}$ sends $a\otimes x$ to $ax$ with inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; hence $F_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], every prime localization of $F_{\mathfrak p}$ is therefore a regular local ring. In Lean use ULift.algEquiv, Module.Finite.of_surjective and AlgEquiv.isPurelyInseparable for this extension, then transport IsRegularRing along Algebra.TensorProduct.congr followed by Algebra.TensorProduct.lid. Only the ring predicates of [def-weil-regular-scheme], already in Mathlib.RingTheory.RegularLocalRing.Defs, are used; no scheme construction is needed.

source.place: Tag 07BZ, definition-regular; geometric regularity in Section 07BY and Algebra Tag 0381, condition (2); preparatory unpacking for Tag 07QK

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Every prime localization $(F_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak r}$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], applied to the regular local rings of step 1. A domain is reduced: if $x^n=0$ for $n\ge1$, induction on $n$ and $x\cdot x^{n-1}=0$ gives $x=0$. Thus all these prime localizations are reduced. Apply the reducedness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective] to the commutative ring $F_{\mathfrak p}$; it follows that $F_{\mathfrak p}$ is reduced. This holds for every prime of $A$, including a zero fibre, for which the family of primes is empty and reducedness still holds.

source.place: Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain; Tag 00HN, lemma-characterize-zero-local, part (1); expansion of the regular-fibre input in More on Algebra Tag 07QK

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced] to the Noetherian reduced ring $A$: it has $(R_0)$ and $(S_1)$. Apply the same equivalence to every $F_{\mathfrak p}$, using its Noetherianity from step 1 and its reducedness from step 2. Thus every fibre has $(R_0)$ and $(S_1)$ as well. These are precisely the two fibre hypotheses required for the ascent lemmas, with indices $0$ and $1$ respectively.

source.place: Tag 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up, proof: reducedness is (R_0) plus (S_1), citing Algebra Tag 031R, lemma-criterion-reduced

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-regularity-rk-goes-up] with $R=A$, $S=B$, and $k=0$. Both rings are Noetherian by hypothesis, the map is flat by step 1, and $A$ and every fibre have $(R_0)$ by step 3. It follows that $B$ has $(R_0)$. Separately use [lem-weil-pbc-serre-sk-goes-up] for the same map with $k=1$: both Noetherian hypotheses and flatness are the same, while step 3 supplies $(S_1)$ for $A$ and every fibre. Therefore $B$ has $(S_1)$. No finite-type or smoothness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up, proof: Algebra Tags 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up) and 0339 (lemma-Sk-goes-up)

proof.text: The ring $B$ is Noetherian by hypothesis and satisfies $(R_0)$ and $(S_1)$ by step 4. The converse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced], now applied to $B$, gives that $B$ is reduced, as required.
